correctness.rationale: For fixed gamma>1, Hilbert-Schmidt sum is sum_{j>=1} j^(1-2gamma)<infinity. The prefix-sum unitary onto the completion of the Dirichlet difference space gives singular-value inverse Rayleigh quotient lambda=q/m. Neumann cutting at M=ceil(R^kappa), kappa>gamma/(gamma-1), controls tail below Lambda up to one exceptional mode by weighted Poincare and codimension-one interlacing. Geometric partition yields o(R) cut and discretization errors; Neumann chain dispersion has eigenvalues 4sin^2(pi*k/(2h)) and phase F(u)=2/pi arcsin(u/2). Integrating block counts and Tonelli yields the exact constant int_0^infty F(x^-gamma)dx=(1/pi)int_0^pi(2sin(theta/2))^-1/gamma dtheta. Monotone spectral inversion gives s_n~C_gamma^gamma n^-gamma, and harmonic asymptotic gives critical residue C_gamma. Independent high-precision beta-integral at gamma=2 yielded C2^2=1.39320392968567686; not a proof of the infinite Weyl law.
